codeReview.summary: The feature added the intended foreign keys and regenerated Drizzle artifacts, but it still leaves `workflow_steps.workflow_pack_id` without an actual SQLite foreign-key constraint even though the schema relations model and domain imply that dependency.

issues.description: `workflow_steps.workflow_pack_id` is still declared as a plain `text(...).notNull()` column instead of referencing `workflow_packs.id`. This orphanable relationship is part of the domain model (`workflowPack` relation exists in the same file), so the feature does not fully satisfy the stated intent to add the missing SQLite foreign-key constraints where the domain implies them. The regenerated migration confirms the FK is still absent from `workflow_steps`.

The regression test proves several orphan-reference failures, but it does not cover the still-unconstrained `workflow_steps.workflow_pack_id` path. Adding a negative case for an orphan workflow step would have exposed the remaining gap directly.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The backend-worker skill says to write failing tests first and to add deterministic migrations, but the worker had to improvise a temporary runtime-compatible Drizzle config helper because the documented workflow does not explain how to run `drizzle-kit generate` against this package's TS/ESM config setup in Docker.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Handoff skillFeedback marks `followedProcedure` false and explains that `drizzle.config.ts/js` imports `./src/config.js`, which was not directly loadable by drizzle-kit in this environment; suggestedChanges asks for a stable mission-approved generation path.

summary: Review failed: most intended relational constraints were added and tested, but `workflow_steps.workflow_pack_id` remains unenforced in both schema and generated SQLite migration, so orphan workflow steps can still persist despite the feature goal.
